story.title: Liverpool score three at Crystal Palace
story.teaser: Three different players scored as the Reds won away
body: Liverpool won away at Crystal Palace in the Premier League. Three different Liverpool players scored.

Alexis Mac Allister scored first with a great header. Dominik Szoboszlai set it up for him. Later, Florian Wirtz finished nicely after a good run down the right by Bradley Barcola. It was the first Premier League goal of the season for both Mac Allister and Wirtz.
Alexander Isak scored the third goal late on, with help from Wirtz. Isak now has seven league goals this season. Palace did score once, from a penalty.
The star of the match was goalkeeper Alisson. He made a stunning reaction save and plenty more important saves after that. BBC Sport gave him a score of 9 and said he was back to his best.

stories.source_title: Forming a band and growing crops: What a year in a simulated Mars mission is really like
stories.excerpt:
Four people have spent 378 days seeing what it would be like to live on Mars...without leaving Earth.

The crew members took part in a simulated mission to the Red Planet, spending just under a year in isolation at Nasa's Johnson Space Center in Houston.

It's Nasa's second Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog, or CHAPEA, mission. The first ended in July 2024.

The exercise is meant to prepare astronauts for future trips to Mars.

The astronauts live in a specially designed habitat.

It's a 1,700-square-foot (158-square-metre), 3D-printed structure with four bedrooms, a dining/living

story.title: A whole year living like it's Mars
story.teaser: Four people lived on 'Mars' without leaving Earth!
body: Four people have spent 378 days living as if they were on Mars, without leaving Earth. The crew finished their pretend mission on Saturday 31 October at Nasa's Johnson Space Center in Houston.

They lived in a special home built by a 3D printer. It had four bedrooms, a living area, a medical room and a vertical farm for growing crops. The mission was a simulation, meant to help astronauts get ready for real trips to Mars.
The crew did science experiments, pretend space walks and coped with losing contact for two weeks. Every sip of water and every shake of salt had to be recorded for Nasa.
Commander Ross Elder said the home was very quiet, with only the hum of fans. He missed the sound of weather and busy streets! So the crew brought instruments and formed a band in their spare time.
Now the four can finally see their friends and family again.

word_to_know.definition: A pretend version of something real, used to practise or learn.

reasons: The story says 'So the crew brought instruments and formed a band', which suggests they formed the band because Ross Elder missed the noise of weather and streets. The source never links the two; it only says the crew brought instruments and practised in their downtime.

stories.excerpt:
We are now more than a quarter of the way through the Premier League season, with each team having played 10 games.

So what can we read into it?

History suggests the answer is quite a lot.

Last season, for instance, the top two - and two of the eventual bottom three - were in the exact spots at this stage that they in finished six months later.

BBC Sport has a look.

Arsenal are top of the table on 27 points - which is higher than the average number of points (23) champions have after 10 games.

In fact, only four teams have taken more points from their first 10 fixtures than the Gunners,

story.title: What the Premier League table tells us
story.teaser: Arsenal lead, but can history tell us who will win?
body: Every team in the Premier League has now played 10 games. BBC Sport looked at history to see what the table can tell us.

Arsenal are top with 27 points. That is more than the average of 23 points that champions have at this stage. Only four teams have had more points after 10 games, and all four went on to win the league.
But there is a funny twist. The only two teams that had exactly 27 points at this stage in the past did not win the title.

Brighton are second with 22 points. Manchester City have 21 and Liverpool have 18. The fewest points a team has had at this stage and still become champions is 18, so Liverpool are still in with a chance.
Last season, 15 of the 20 teams finished within three places of where they were after 10 games. Still, there is plenty of time for surprises.

story.teaser: Every team has played 10 games. What happens next?

History can give us clues. Only four teams have won more points than Arsenal after 10 games, and all four went on to win the league. The average for champions at this stage is 23 points.

stories.source_title: 'The worst conditions in my 35-year career' - commentating in the FA Cup fog
stories.excerpt:
One of the most important attributes for a commentator is to be able to see the action you are trying to describe but that became a luxury for BBC Sport's Steve Bower when Altrincham hosted Notts County in an FA Cup tie on Saturday.

As thick fog enveloped the Moss Lane ground, he could barely see what was going on in a first-round game being televised live on BBC Two.

"One of the more challenging of my long career, that's about 35 years now," said Bower about the experience.

"I was reminded by a colleague - maybe I'm a jinx - that we had a similar thing on the BBC about three years ago when

story.title: Fog swallows an FA Cup football match
story.teaser: Fog so thick that nobody could see the ball!
body: Thick fog rolled into a football ground on Saturday during an FA Cup match between Altrincham and Notts County. It was so thick that people could barely see the game!
Steve Bower was the BBC commentator. He said it was one of the hardest games of his 35-year career. After about the 60th minute, he could not even tell which team had the ball.
The players had to change how they played. Instead of long passes, they used short ones because they could not see far. Some players said they could not see both goals from the centre circle.

Altrincham led 2-1, but Notts County scored late and the game went to extra-time. Notts County won on penalties. Steve had to listen to the crowd's cheers to work out what had happened. He said it was a unique evening!

word_to_know.definition: A person who describes what is happening in a match for people watching or listening.

Altrincham led 2-1, but Notts County equalised late on. The game went to extra-time, and Notts County won on penalties.

Players said they could not see both goals from the centre circle. They played short passes instead of long ones. Fans at the far end had to listen to the crowd to know what was happening. Some Altrincham fans even shone their phone lights in the fog.

story.title: The football match played in thick fog
story.teaser: Commentators and players could barely see the ball!
body: A football match in the FA Cup was almost called off because of incredibly thick fog. The game was between Altrincham and Notts County at Altrincham's Moss Lane ground on Saturday, and it was shown live on BBC Two.

BBC commentator Steve Bower, who has been describing matches for 35 years, said it was one of the hardest games of his whole career. Once the ball went near the centre circle, he could not see a thing. He could not even tell which team had it!

The players struggled too. They had to stop playing long passes and use short ones instead, because they could not see their team-mates far away. Some players said they could not see both goals or the corner flags.
Altrincham were leading 2-1, but Notts County equalised late on and won the game on penalties. Bower said it will be a match people remember for a very long time.

stories.source_title: Print commissioned by Nasa uncovered for exhibition
stories.excerpt:
A print by a Yorkshire artist commissioned by Nasa in the early days of space travel will go on show as part of a pop art exhibition.

Komtek I by Michael Fossick, who studied at Bradford School of Art, was created in 1962 to celebrate a Hong Kong company that produced microcomputers in the early days of space travel.

The print was part of a Nasa project to document the effort of sending the first humans to the moon and is on display as part of the Pop Art at Cartwright Hall exhibition.

The display tells the story of the British International Print Biennale, which took place at the Bradford

story.title: Space-age art made for Nasa goes on show
story.teaser: A Yorkshire artist made a print for Nasa in 1962!
body: A picture made for Nasa in the early days of space travel is going on show at Cartwright Hall, an art gallery in Bradford. It is called Komtek I. It was made in 1962 by an artist called Michael Fossick.
In March 1962, Nasa asked 38 artists, including Fossick, to make art about its work. Nasa was trying to send the first humans to the moon. Neil Armstrong stepped on the moon in 1969.
Fossick's print celebrates Komtek I, a small computer from Hong Kong that was important in the early space programme. The print was made from a very early computer image.
In 1968, the print won a prize at a big art show at Cartwright Hall. The new exhibition tells the story of that show and runs until March 2027.
The curator, Jill Iredale, said it was a bizarre connection that an artist from Sheffield was asked to work for Nasa.

body: A piece of art made for Nasa, the American space agency, is going on display in Bradford. The print is called Komtek I and was made by artist Michael Fossick, who went to Bradford School of Art.

In 1962, Nasa asked 38 artists to help record its work as it prepared to send the first humans to the moon. Fossick was one of them. His bright screen print celebrated an early microcomputer used in the space programme.
The artwork is part of a pop art exhibition at Cartwright Hall, which also includes work by famous artists Andy Warhol and David Hockney.
Curator Jill Iredale said it was a "completely bizarre" link between a Yorkshire artist and Nasa. The exhibition runs until March 2027.

story.title: Nasa print found in Bradford gallery
story.teaser: A pop art print made for Nasa in 1962 is going on show in Bradford.
body: A print made for Nasa in the early days of space travel is going on show in Bradford.
The print is called Komtek I. It was created in 1962 by Michael Fossick, an artist who studied at Bradford School of Art.
Nasa asked 38 artists to make work about its space achievements. Fossick chose to celebrate a microcomputer that was important in the early years of the space programme.
The print is part of the Pop Art at Cartwright Hall exhibition. It tells the story of the British International Print Biennale, which took place at the gallery between 1968 and 1990.
The exhibition runs until March 2027. It also includes work by famous artists Andy Warhol and David Hockney.

word_to_know.definition: a small computer, especially one from the early days of computing
